Full biography & original profile details

My group takes AI inspection out of the lab and into aircraft manufacturing and maintenance, from the camera to the robot to the certified record.

I have collaborated with aerospace companies in the UAE since 2014, developing automation and inspection approaches for efficient and sustainable aerospace operations.

The work runs across four connected threads: AI-enabled visual inspection, non-destructive testing with infrared thermography, robotic and smart industrial systems, and blockchain-based traceability for inspection data. Research interests also include immersive technologies (VR, MR and AR). Partners include Sanad Aerotech, COMAC, SILAL and Beijing Institute of Technology, and the same methods now reach into precision agriculture.

Our publications are cited 92% above the world average for the field (SciVal, 2022–2025), and the 2023 review that set our roadmap ranks in the top 1% worldwide by field-weighted citation impact.

  • PositionAssistant Professor, Aerospace Engineering, Khalifa University, with a dual affiliation in Management Science and Engineering
  • LeadershipDeputy Director, Advanced Research and Innovation Center (ARIC); KU Lead, SAMC–KU NDT Joint Lab
  • LabFounder, Transformative Aerospace Lab (2024): infrared thermography rigs, a robotic inspection cell and a blade sample library
  • EducationPhD in Interdisciplinary Engineering (2020) and MSc in Engineering Systems and Management (2016), Masdar Institute in collaboration with MIT; BSc with honors in Engineering Management (2011), University of Arizona
  • EarlierUAE National Postdoctoral Fellow, Khalifa University (2022–2023); Demand-Side Management Engineer, ADDC / TAQA (2019–2022)
  • DistinctionFirst Emirati woman to hold a faculty position in aerospace engineering in the UAE

Bio-inspired flight draws on the supplied wing-modelling project. Current viscous-flow trials use prescribed rigid-wing motion; two-way fluid–structure coupling and aerodynamic validation remain research tasks.

Original research roadmap & reported metrics
01

A roadmap, then the work

In 2023 we mapped what was stopping AI inspection from reaching the hangar. Since then, each project has tackled one of those problems.

Top 1%

of papers worldwide by field-weighted citation impact

Aero-engine blade defect detection: a systematic review of deep learning models

IEEE Access, 2023. A review of more than a hundred studies that organised the field by method, imaging modality and defect type, named the barriers to industrial use — scarce training data, the gap between simulation and reality, no shared benchmarks, and no deployed end-to-end systems — and set out the roadmap the group has followed since.

Problem: real, labelled images of damaged blades are almost impossible to collect at scale.

BladeSynth

A physics-based rendering pipeline that turns CAD blade models into realistic inspection images with synthetic defects and pixel-perfect labels. Models trained on it work on real blade images.

Scientific Data, 2025. Read paper ↗

Openpublic dataset and pipeline
Usedto train our deployed system

Problem: no published system covered the whole job, from picking up a blade to reporting its defects.

Robotic blade inspection

A robot finds each blade in a container, picks it up, images it, runs deep-learning defect detection and puts it back, built for maintenance-shop workflows.

Scientific Reports, 2026. Read paper ↗

~4 sper blade
88.2%mean average precision
1,290downloads in 3 months

Problem: thermography methods analyse each processed view of the heat signal on its own and miss what they show together.

PT-Fusion

A deep-learning model that fuses two standard pulse-thermography representations to find defects in composites and estimate how deep they are, with fewer parameters than leading transformer models.

Scientific Reports, 2026. Read paper ↗Code ↗

10%more accurate than U-Net-style baselines
Opencode and trained models

Problem: regulators need tamper-proof inspection records, but AI results are probabilistic and hard to audit.

BladeChain

A blockchain network shared by manufacturer, airline, maintenance shop and regulator. Every inspection records which AI model and version made the call, and new inspections trigger automatically on flight hours or cycles.

Scientific Reports, 2026. Read paper ↗

100%of lifecycle events captured
17 msto detect tampering

All partnerships, deployment details & original claims
02

With industry

Research shaped by partners' real problems, and tested on their shop floors.

From the lab to the hangar

With Sanad Aerotech, a Mubadala company, we built inspection systems for aero-engine blades and took them into a working maintenance shop.

  • Two prototypes, robotic blade sorting and automated chord measurement, soft-deployed at Sanad Aerotech
  • The automated chord measurement system was approved by Lufthansa Technik Middle East
  • Co-founder of Stride Robotic Technologies, a robotics start-up on the Khalifa Innovation Center seed track

AI visual defect detection, TRL 6

97.9%detection accuracy
78 µmmeasurement precision
35%shorter inspection cycle

9th COMAC International Science & Technology Innovation Week, Shanghai, September 2026

1stArab-region institution to co-organise, alongside COMAC and NUAA

The first COMAC partnership in the Middle East

I built and coordinate Khalifa University's collaboration with COMAC through Shanghai Aircraft Manufacturing Co. (SAMC): KU's first aerospace partnership with China and COMAC's first in the Arab region.

  • A joint SAMC–KU NDT Joint Lab at Khalifa University, which I lead
  • A sponsored programme in rapid damage detection for composite aircraft structures, now running
  • Three research directions agreed with SAMC: robotic visual and infrared inspection, inspection and remaining-life prediction around drilled holes, and trusted inspection data
  • A competitive call I organised that opened funded COMAC projects to three more KU research teams

The university profile lists three SANAD Aerotech and Mubadala Aerospace Company projects for January–December 2024, with Dr. Abdulrahman as Principal Investigator: automated blade sorting, automated chord measurement and aerospace engine blade inspection. The blade sorting system combines a robotic arm, load cell, AI vision and a sorting algorithm; chord measurement uses a robotic arm, laser profiler and ROS interface; surface inspection combines synthetic and real training data with autonomous robotic image acquisition. An additional internally funded KU project integrates infrared thermography and emerging technologies for aerospace NDT.

More partnerships

Smart farming · SILAL

AI for the farm

Plant AI and AerialYield are university-listed projects in collaboration with Silal, supported by external funding. Related work includes AgriDrone for crop yield and ripeness, a phone app that spots strawberry disease, an automated pollination device and a wearable sensor that feels fruit firmness.

UAE–China

Intelligent manufacturing lab

KU lead on the UAE–China Joint Research Laboratory in Intelligent Manufacturing with Beijing Institute of Technology.

Air Q

Opening doors for colleagues

As KU's coordinator for the Air Q aerospace partnership, I have enabled three research projects led by other KU faculty, from quiet quadcopters to cloud-seeding drones.

Teaching, mentoring & recognition: full original details
03

Teaching and mentoring

Students learn best on real problems, with practising engineers in the room.

New course

NDT and failure analysis of aerospace structures

A senior elective, co-designed with Prof. Kin Liao, and the department's first course to pair NDT theory with hands-on work on industrial-class infrared thermography rigs.

Senior design

12 industry-linked project teams

Capstone projects with Sanad Aerotech, Strata Manufacturing, The Exploration Company and Droneleaf, in inspection, robotics, drones and manufacturing.

RISE

Real Industry Scenarios and Experiences

A programme I founded that pairs students and early-career women with senior industry mentors. It was cited in KU's Best Educational Institution in Aviation award, Women in Aviation Middle East, 2025.

Two PhD students graduated in 2026, one under my primary supervision and one co-supervised. I also teach Research Methods in Engineering, Quality and Reliability Engineering, and Leadership and Professional Development. The university profile lists Quality Control & Reliability (ISYE311), Research Methods in HSE (ENGR701), Senior Design Project I (AERO497), Senior Design Project 2 (AERO498), Special Topics in AERO (AERO395), and Nondestructive Testing and Failure Analysis of Aerospace Structures.
